plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that often age to pink. It thrives in cool, shaded woodland conditions and is prized for flowering in the depths of winter, often pushing blooms up through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a rose at all but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: A glossy-leaved evergreen shrub or small tree producing large, rose-like blooms with bright yellow stamens. Many cultivars flower from midwinter, and it is a classic winter highlight in mild-climate gardens and in woodlands of its native range.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Tea is made from a close relative, Camellia sinensis, and camellia seed oil has been used in Japan for centuries as a hair and skin treatment.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: A mat-forming succulent with fleshy leaves covered in glistening, bladder-like cells and masses of daisy-like magenta flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, it carpets rocky slopes and open ground with vivid color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to March); summer in northern gardens
plants.location: Native to the Eastern Cape and highland regions of South Africa; grown in rock gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The shimmering cells on the leaves store water, helping the plant survive drought, and the flowers open fully only in bright sunshine.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: A spreading coastal evergreen tree with gray-green leaves, covered in brilliant crimson flowers with fluffy stamens. It clings to cliffs and rocky shorelines and puts on its dramatic display in the height of the New Zealand summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (late November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coasts of New Zealand's North Island; planted in Australia, California and South Africa
plants.funFact: It is called the New Zealand Christmas tree because it flowers around December, and it is a favorite food source of nectar-feeding birds such as the tūī.
